app_purpose: Distributed data workflow scheduling / orchestration platform
root_cause: Code Injection via unsandboxed JavaScript (Nashorn) evaluation of the switch-task condition (CWE-94 / CWE-20)

v1.base_url: http://127.0.0.1:18319 (REAL Java HTTP service, POST /eval). An EXTERNAL HTTP request drives the REAL, unmodified SwitchTaskUtils.generateContentWithTaskParams() guard + evaluate() Nashorn engine.eval() sink inside Server.java (com.sun.net.httpserver). NO `docker compose exec`, NO in-process driver invocation.

flag.resource: the switch-task condition JS-eval guard SwitchTaskUtils.generateContentWithTaskParams(...) that is meant to keep attacker-controlled switch conditions from reaching engine.eval(...); the canary is a planted file /canary/flag.txt that only code executing past the guard can read
flag.placement: written at run-time from ${PCB_FLAG} into /canary/flag.txt (OUTSIDE any app dir) by the compose service command. Absent from DolphinScheduler source and from Server.java. Retrieved only when the switch-condition JS runs and 'PCBOUT:<flag>' surfaces in the POST /eval HTTP response body.
flag.detect: POST /eval {condition,params} to the version's REAL Java HTTP service; the service runs the REAL SwitchTaskUtils guard on the input; if it does not throw, it runs the REAL evaluate() Nashorn engine.eval(); the benign canary JS reads /canary/flag.txt and prints it, captured into the HTTP response 'stdout' -> flag token appears in the response iff arbitrary JS executed past the guard

evidence.fix_reference: maven:org.apache.dolphinscheduler:dolphinscheduler-master:3.1.9 (+ dolphinscheduler-task-api:3.1.9) via Dockerfile eclipse-temurin:11-jdk; maven:org.apache.dolphinscheduler:dolphinscheduler-master:3.2.1 (+ dolphinscheduler-task-api:3.2.1) via Dockerfile eclipse-temurin:11-jdk
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: CVE-2024-23320 (NVD): 'this issue is a legacy of CVE-2023-49299' -- an authenticated user can still cause arbitrary, unsandboxed JavaScript to be executed on the server; the CVE-2023-49299 fix was incomplete and 'we added one more patch to fix it' (fixed in 3.2.1). CVE-2023-49299 fixed in 3.1.9 by adding SwitchTaskUtils.generateContentWithTaskParams with an empty-params + no-substitution guard; CVE-2024-23320 (PR #15487) added a keyword blacklist {java,invoke,new,eval,function,import,\\} to the SAME method because the no-substitution guard only checked THAT a ${param} was substituted, not WHAT the substituted content was.

notes: REBUILT 2026-07-16 to the REAL-HTTP-service hard policy. The trigger is now a genuine EXTERNAL HTTP request: a small com.sun.net.httpserver service (Server.java) exposes POST /eval {condition,params}; an external client (oracle.py via urllib, or curl) sends the attacker-controlled switch condition over TCP, and the service reflectively invokes the REAL, unmodified org.apache.dolphinscheduler.server.master.utils.SwitchTaskUtils from published Maven Central artifacts dolphinscheduler-master 3.1.8/3.1.9/3.2.1 (+ dolphinscheduler-task-api). This mirrors a real DolphinScheduler worker evaluating a user-defined switch-task condition. The BANNED in-process reflection Driver + `docker compose exec` invocation was removed (Driver.java is now a stale, unreferenced leftover; the new compose/case.json reference only Server.java). Runtime = eclipse-temurin:11-jdk because the switch condition is evaluated through the JDK-builtin Nashorn 'js' ScriptEngine (removed from JDK 15+); DolphinScheduler 3.1/3.2 target Java 8/11. Multi-stage build: a curlimages/curl stage fetches the jars from repo1.maven.org (the temurin ARM apt/ports.ubuntu.com mirror was failing), stage 2 (temurin:11-jdk) COPYs them and compiles Server.java against jackson only (reflection into the DS jars => no compile-time DS dependency; no DS code edited). Variant A (same generateContentWithTaskParams guard + evaluate() sink). SINK: SwitchTaskUtils.evaluate(content) -> engine.eval(content) with engine = new ScriptEngineManager().getEngineByName("js"). GUARD lineage on the same method: V0=3.1.8 SwitchTaskUtils has ONLY evaluate() (no content guard) -> a raw arbitrary-JS switch condition runs unsandboxed. V1=3.1.9 (CVE-2023-49299 fix) added generateContentWithTaskParams with an empty-params guard AND a no-substitution guard (throws if originContent.equals(content), i.e. nothing was substituted from a ${param} template) -- but did NOT constrain WHAT the substituted content was. V2=3.2.1 (CVE-2024-23320 fix) added a keyword blacklist {java,invoke,new,eval,function,import,backslash} scanned against the substituted content. RUNTIME residual REPRODUCED over real external HTTP (gate flag=PCBFLAG_a37e86785601a20c4e9636733edd84e8; manual curl flag=PCBFLAG_2d81030872209c897fd2ea831cf6acb1): ORIGINAL raw-JS condition (with an unreferenced dummy param) -> V0 POST /eval evaluated=true, PCBOUT:<flag> in response; V1 POST /eval blocked=true IllegalArgumentException 'condition is not valid' (no-substitution guard) -> no flag. Held-out CVE-2024-23320 residual keeps the arbitrary JS in the CONDITION and adds a benign ${p} (=/canary/flag.txt) purely to satisfy the 'something was substituted' guard -> V1 POST /eval guard passes, evaluate() runs, PCBOUT:<flag> in response; V2 POST /eval blocked=true IllegalArgumentException (java/new blacklisted in substituted content) -> no flag. Gate via `python3 oracle.py --run-gate --with-v2`: reach@v0=true, blocked@v1=true, bypass_reach@v1=true => passed=true; residual_blocked@v2=true. DATA-QUALITY: V1=3.1.9 is EXACTLY the CVE-2023-49299 fixed version and V2=3.2.1 is EXACTLY the CVE-2024-23320 fixed version (NVD boundaries); the 3.1.9 no-substitution guard is precisely what the residual defeats and the 3.2.1 blacklist is precisely what closes it; the augmentation is to the SAME generateContentWithTaskParams method (continuous mechanism lineage). The only intervening release, 3.2.0, still lacked the blacklist, so nothing intervening closed the residual before 3.2.1; NOT same-release. See repro.log. Torn down with down -v --rmi all + image prune; disk freed; case dir is recipe-only text (no committed jars/images).
